title: Banneker Ventures Secures $20 Million Loan from Amazon
summary: Banneker Ventures, a Black-led construction firm, has obtained a $20 million loan from Amazon's Housing Equity Fund to construct an affordable housing project in Prince George’s County. The $45 million project will include 193 affordable housing units in Capitol Heights, with completion expected by 2025. This loan is crucial for the project, as stated by Banneker Ventures' founder Omar A. Karim, and the units will remain affordable for 99 years, targeting households earning 40% to 60% of the median regional income.

title: Can you spot a fake website? Slowing down can save you from being scammed
summary: A study found that slowing down can significantly reduce the chances of falling victim to online scams, especially those involving fake websites. Scammers often create a sense of urgency to prevent careful evaluation, and participants given less time performed worse at identifying fake sites. The research suggests that analytical reasoning and deliberate action, rather than quick emotional responses, are key to distinguishing legitimate websites from fraudulent ones.

title: 5G Future Forum accelerating 5G and Edge Compute solutions around the world
summary: The 5G Future Forum (5GFF) demonstrated a first-of-its-kind music collaboration using its Edge Discovery Service (EDS) API, allowing guitarists in New York, Toronto, and London to sync their performance. This showcase, powered by Amazon Web Services, Rogers, Verizon, and Vodafone, highlights the potential of 5G and mobile edge compute technology for transforming global communication and collaboration. Rogers, a founding member of 5GFF, expressed pride in accelerating the delivery of these technologies.

title: OALC Top Holdings List & Exposure (OneAscent Large Cap Core ETF)
summary: This article details the top holdings and exposure of the OneAscent Large Cap Core ETF (OALC), an equity fund focusing on large-cap strategies in North America. It lists the top 25 stock holdings, including NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Amazon.com, which collectively represent nearly 50% of the fund. The ETF's geographic, currency, sector, and industry exposures, primarily in the United States and technology, are also outlined.

title: IWV Top Holdings List & Exposure (iShares Russell 3000 ETF)
summary: This article details the top holdings of the iShares Russell 3000 ETF (IWV), an equity fund investing in publicly traded companies primarily in North America. The top 25 holdings are listed by weight, with NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft leading. It also provides a breakdown of IWV's geographic, currency, sector, and industry exposures, showing a significant concentration in the United States and the Technology sector.

title: Amazon Business Launches 3-Way Match for Mobile App
summary: Amazon Business has launched a 3-Way Match feature on its mobile app, allowing users to scan package barcodes to automatically mark items as received. This new tool, available in the U.S., helps businesses improve procurement, automate reporting, and ensure accuracy in purchase payments by matching purchase orders, invoices, and receipts from anywhere at no additional cost. The feature aims to streamline processes, save time, and reduce the risk of incorrect or fraudulent payments.

title: Tesla union labor battle shows need for church’s leadership and teaching voice
summary: A labor dispute at Tesla's Buffalo plant, where employees allege retaliatory firings for unionizing efforts, highlights the need for the Catholic Church to reassert its social teaching on labor rights. Despite general public approval for unions, membership rates are historically low nationwide. The article argues that the Catholic Church, with its rich history of advocating for workers' rights, has a crucial role to play in guiding the modern labor movement.

title: 8 in-demand creative skills for freelancers―many can pay more than $100 per hour
summary: Freelancing remains a popular career choice in the U.S., with many workers planning to continue or start freelancing in 2023. While tech and marketing skills are in demand, creative skills also offer significant opportunities, with some paying over $100 per hour. Upwork identified eight top in-demand creative skills for freelancers this year, including graphic design, video editing, 3D animation, and product design.

title: VT vs ACWI ETF: Which is the Best World ETF?
summary: This article compares two popular World ETFs, Vanguard's Total World Stock Index Fund ETF (VT) and iShares' MSCI ACWI ETF (ACWI), to help investors decide which is best for their portfolio. It delves into their differences in expense ratios, underlying indices, geographical breakdown, number of constituents, dividend yields, and fund managers, as well as their similarities in strategy, purpose, returns, liquidity, and sector breakdown. The author concludes that VT offers a lower expense ratio and exposure to smaller-cap companies, which might appeal to investors seeking that longer-tail exposure.

title: Amazon delays HQ2's second phase in Pentagon City, updates hiring count
summary: Amazon has delayed the second phase of its HQ2 buildout, known as PenPlace, in Pentagon City. Despite this delay, the company reaffirms its commitment to hire 25,000 employees at HQ2. This update comes amidst previous decisions by Amazon to vacate office spaces and adjust return-to-office plans.

title: Amazon is pushing back construction on Arlington-based HQ2
summary: Amazon has announced it is pausing construction on the second phase of its HQ2 in Arlington, Virginia, known as PenPlace. While the first phase, Metropolitan Park, is set to open this summer, the company cited the need to evaluate space plans and sufficient capacity in Metropolitan Park for 14,000 employees as reasons for the delay. This decision follows recent layoffs and a new return-to-work policy requiring employees to be in the office three days a week.

title: Amazon delays construction on HQ2 in Northern Virginia
summary: Amazon has announced delays in the construction of its HQ2 in Northern Virginia, specifically impacting the PenPlace phase. Despite the construction delay, the company still intends to hire 25,000 employees for the HQ2 project. The updated timeline for PenPlace remains uncertain.

title: Best Buy, Walmart, other major US retailers tout health services
summary: Major U.S. retailers like Best Buy, Walmart, and Amazon are expanding into healthcare and health-related products as inflation-wary Americans prioritize services over goods. Best Buy has partnered with Atrium Health for a hospital-at-home program, Walmart announced new health centers, and Amazon acquired One Medical. This strategic shift aims to tap into the resilient healthcare market and offset declining discretionary spending on electronics and other goods.

title: The Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show Returns to TV in September
summary: The Victoria's Secret Fashion Show is returning in September after a four-year hiatus, rebranded as "The Tour." This new iteration aims to be a fashion event and documentary celebrating women and global creatives, streaming on Prime Video. The show seeks to address past controversies by emphasizing inclusivity, featuring a mix of returning "Angels" and newcomers, and allowing viewers to shop pieces inspired by the event.

title: Sprouts' latest real estate strategy means WA grocery store closure
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market announced it would be closing grocery stores in Washington, Texas, California, Georgia, and Florida, as part of its latest real estate strategy. The Phoenix-based specialty grocery chain is implementing these closures across multiple states. This move reflects a broader strategic shift for the company.

title: Walmart will derive more profit from services, ad sales in next 5 years -CFO
summary: Walmart expects its future profitability to increasingly come from advertising sales on Walmart.com and fees from its online marketplace and delivery services, rather than traditional merchandise sales. CFO John David Rainey stated that these higher-margin, faster-growing segments will significantly shift the company's profit composition over the next five years. This strategic pivot mirrors other major retailers investing in retail media and third-party marketplaces.

title: Amazon worker loses bid for California class action over remote work expenses
summary: A U.S. District Judge in San Francisco denied a class action lawsuit against Amazon seeking reimbursement for remote work expenses for nearly 7,000 California workers. The judge stated that the plaintiff failed to prove a company-wide policy of non-reimbursement, noting that many workers had received some reimbursement. The denial was without prejudice, allowing the plaintiff to refile with a revised class.

title: News | Salesforce Executive Calls In-Office Work Critical to Tech Giant’s Profitability
summary: Salesforce's Chief Operating Officer Brian Millham states that in-person work is crucial for the company's future growth and profitability, reversing a previous stance on remote work. He noted a drop in productivity among remote employees during the pandemic. The company's shift back to a hybrid model, requiring sales and service employees in the office four days a week, appears to be positively impacting revenue growth.

title: Microsoft adding to far West Side data center with $175.9 million expansion project this year
summary: Microsoft is planning a $175.9 million expansion of its data center in San Antonio's Texas Research Park, dubbed "SAT40." Construction on the 153,227-square-foot facility is set to begin in June and finish in September 2023. This is the latest in a series of data center investments by Microsoft in the area, driven by increasing demand for cloud technology despite recent company-wide layoffs.

title: What Are Optimization Problems? How QCI’s Unique Quantum Approach Can Help Organizations Solve Complex Problems Across Industries
summary: This article explains optimization problems, which involve finding the best solution given various constraints, and how businesses can benefit from solving them. It highlights why quantum computers, specifically QCI's Dirac devices with their qudit approach, are well-suited to tackle these complex problems that often exceed the capabilities of classical computers. The piece details QCI's successful application in real-world scenarios, such as optimizing sensor placement for BMW and supply chain logistics, and discusses the future of quantum solutions in achieving quantum advantage for difficult business challenges.

title: Why Doesn’t Airbnb Have a Loyalty Program?
summary: Despite users expressing interest and a past announcement of a "Superguest" program in 2018, Airbnb has not implemented a loyalty program. The company's significant success and strong market position, coupled with a lack of reliance on business travelers who typically drive loyalty programs, are cited as key reasons for this absence. For frequent travelers seeking rewards, hotel loyalty programs remain a viable alternative.

title: Chinese MRO procurement platform ZKH Group files for $200M US IPO
summary: ZKH Group Ltd, a Chinese maintenance repair and operations (MRO) procurement service platform, has filed with the SEC for an initial public offering in the US, aiming to raise up to $200 million. The Shanghai-based company plans to list on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol "ZKH". This IPO, underwritten by Goldman Sachs and China Renaissance, would be the largest US IPO from a Chinese issuer since October 2021.

title: Chinese MRO procurement platform ZKH Group files for $200M US IPO
summary: ZKH Group Ltd, a Chinese maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) procurement service platform, has filed for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) in the US, aiming to raise up to $200 million. The Shanghai-based company plans to list on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker "ZKH," with Goldman Sachs and China Renaissance acting as joint underwriters. If successful, this would be the largest US IPO by a Chinese issuer since October 2021.

title: Southwest Airlines Partners With Amazon After the Colossal Mess That Was Late 2022
summary: After its significant operational meltdown in late 2022, Southwest Airlines has announced a partnership with Amazon Web Services (AWS). This collaboration aims to enhance Southwest's reliability by using AWS for ticket booking, flight operations optimization, customer interactions, and crew scheduling. The airline hopes this technological upgrade will prevent future travel disruptions and improve overall efficiency.

title: QVC launches accessible and adaptive products line with Selma Blair
summary: QVC has launched "Accessible Living," a new on-air show and product category dedicated to home products that facilitate everyday tasks and independent living. Actress Selma Blair, who lives with MS, has partnered with QVC as the brand ambassador for this initiative.

title: You can now buy a QLED Roku 4K TV that’s actually made by Roku
summary: Roku has launched its first Roku-branded QLED 4K TVs, available exclusively at Best Buy in the US. These new TVs come in two series, Plus and Select, offering screen sizes from 24 to 75 inches, with the Plus series featuring QLED technology, local dimming, Dolby Vision/HDR10+, and Dolby Atmos-certified speakers. Roku is also updating its OS with personalized news and sports experiences, and enhancing its mobile app with expanded features, positioning itself as a strong competitor in the affordable smart TV market against brands like Amazon.

title: 3 Amazing AI Stocks for Your March Buy List
summary: This article highlights three AI stocks – Dynatrace (DT), Check Point (CHKP), and Schrodinger (SDGR) – as excellent investment opportunities for March. The author argues that artificial intelligence's growing power and impact across sectors like healthcare and IT will lead to significant profitability for companies utilizing strong AI technologies. Each company is presented with details on how their AI solutions are driving growth and why they are considered strong investments.

title: Sonos Bets on Spatial Audio as a Key Brand Differentiator
summary: Sonos is positioning spatial audio as a critical differentiator with its new Era 100 and Era 300 speakers. The Era 300 is the first Sonos speaker to support spatial audio, delivering an immersive 3D audio experience tailored for movie and TV content, and is anticipated to be a definitive way to listen to spatial audio mixes. The company believes embracing spatial audio will solidify its leadership in the premium audio market, even as wider streaming support for the technology is still developing.

title: Big Tech Has Layoffs All Wrong
summary: This article argues that the recent wave of layoffs in Big Tech companies is a misguided and conventional approach, contrary to their self-proclaimed innovative management styles. It suggests that these staff cuts, often driven by investor expectations and a desire to reassert power over workers, are detrimental to long-term financial performance and employee morale. The author proposes alternative strategies like "secondment" programs and furloughs, highlighting that many profitable tech giants have suitable alternatives to mass dismissals.

title: Zero trust illustrated: Secure cloud migration
summary: This article focuses on securing cloud migrations using a zero-trust architecture (ZTA), emphasizing posture control and secure workload communications. It highlights the importance of protecting against misconfigurations, vulnerabilities, and threats in cloud-native applications, advocating for early security integration in the software development lifecycle. The piece stresses that robust zero-trust protection must extend beyond user access to encompass the security of applications and workloads themselves.

title: Airbnb Could Generate $1.2 Billion With Sponsored Listings and an Ad Platform by 2026
summary: Airbnb is exploring launching sponsored listings and an advertising platform, a move that could generate an estimated $1.2 billion in revenue by 2026. CEO Brian Chesky noted that competitors like Expedia and Booking.com already earn significant advertising revenue, highlighting the "massive opportunity" for Airbnb to increase its take rate. This initiative follows similar successful strategies by e-commerce giants and other travel platforms.

title: Is NH ‘immune’ from tech layoffs?
summary: Despite widespread tech layoffs across the nation, particularly in the Boston area, New Hampshire's tech sector remains relatively stable. While other states have seen thousands of job cuts, NH companies like Fidelity, Red River Computer, and Extreme Networks are actively hiring. Experts suggest that NH businesses were either more cautious in their hiring or constrained by existing workforce shortages, avoiding the over-hiring that led to mass layoffs elsewhere.

title: Microsoft Details How Enterprises Can Use ChatGPT with Up-to-Date, Non-Public Corporate Data
summary: Microsoft has outlined how enterprises can leverage ChatGPT with their current, non-public corporate data, addressing the chatbot's September 2021 knowledge cutoff. The solution integrates Azure OpenAI Service with Azure Cognitive Search, allowing ChatGPT to generate responses based on up-to-date internal information. The company also detailed methods for validating responses, such as citations and access to supporting content.

title: Niu's KQi3 Max Escooter Is a Heavy but Reliable Ride
summary: The Niu KQi3 Max escooter is reviewed as a reliable and well-balanced ride, despite being a heavy but minor upgrade over its predecessor, the KQi3 Pro. It offers a powerful 450-watt motor, solid range, comfortable handling for taller riders, and a unique folding mechanism. While it has some drawbacks like lack of turn signals and app-dependent speed settings, its overall performance and sturdy build make it a dependable choice for daily commutes, especially in hilly areas or for heavier riders.

title: The 10 highest paid people in cloud networking
summary: The article lists the top 10 highest-paid executives in the cloud networking industry, detailing their salaries, stock awards, and contributions to their respective companies. It highlights that while base salaries have remained steady for most, significant bonuses and stock awards have led to multi-million dollar paydays, especially for those instrumental in growing cloud and AI divisions. Andrew Jassy of Amazon tops the list with $212 million, largely from stock awards.

title: Yeti recalling close to 2 million coolers and gear cases
summary: Yeti is recalling nearly two million coolers and gear cases due to a defect where high-powered magnets in the closures can detach, posing a risk of serious injury or death. The affected products include the YETI Hopper M30 Soft Cooler 1.0 and 2.0, Hopper M20 Soft Backpack Cooler, and SideKick Dry Gear Case. Consumers are advised to immediately stop using these products and contact Yeti for refund information, although no magnet ingestions or injuries have been reported.

title: Four Ways to Cluster based on Correlation
summary: This article explores four methods to cluster 20 companies based on the correlation of their stock prices. It aims to see if these methods can accurately classify companies into categories like tech or oil and gas, as an alternative to clustering based on raw stock prices. The objective is to validate whether correlation-based clustering reveals meaningful industry groupings.

title: Evolution of Primary Care Delivery
summary: The article discusses the evolving landscape of primary care delivery, driven by an aging population, the growth of Medicare Advantage and other value-based payment models, and digital transformation. It highlights the increasing role of insurers and retail providers in primary care, physician consolidation and shortages, and the innovations in care models focusing on improved patient outcomes and cost reduction. The author emphasizes that the future of primary care will be supported by technology and incentivized by value-based payments, requiring strategic adaptation from healthcare providers.

title: Southwest Airlines moves to AWS
summary: Southwest Airlines is migrating its applications to Amazon Web Services (AWS) as part of a digital transformation initiative. This move aims to enhance passenger experience, improve operational efficiency, and optimize IT infrastructure resource allocation, covering everything from ticket purchases to flight operations. The decision follows a major technological breakdown in December 2022 that disrupted the airline's operations.

title: Bakkt Theater to replace Zappos Theater name at Planet Hollywood
summary: The showroom at Planet Hollywood, formerly known as Zappos Theater, will be renamed Bakkt Theater. This change comes as Bakkt Holdings, Inc., a technology platform for crypto and loyalty, solidifies its relationship with Caesars Entertainment. The partnership aims to integrate Bakkt Crypto Rewards into the Caesars Rewards program, offering new crypto options to customers.

title: Inside Best Buy’s big bet on the Home
summary: This article examines Best Buy's growing involvement in the healthcare sector, particularly its strategy to enable rather than directly provide care in the home, leveraging its Geek Squad and Current Health acquisition. The company is partnering with major health systems on hospital-at-home initiatives, aiming for future growth in its Health division. The piece also briefly touches on the Silicon Valley Bank crisis and other health tech, finance, and policy updates.

title: Smart move: Artificial intelligence and 3D laser scanning for MEP applications
summary: This article explores how artificial intelligence (AI) and 3D laser scanning can significantly benefit Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) applications. It highlights how 3D laser scanning provides crucial accurate data for new construction or retrofitting projects, while AI can then process this data for pattern recognition, identifying optimal and energy-efficient solutions, and enhancing project management. The combination of these technologies, along with human expertise, is presented as a powerful tool for improving efficiency and decision-making in MEP design and implementation.

title: Amazon to Test Satellite Internet Service Starting Next Year
summary: Amazon plans to begin beta testing its Project Kuiper satellite internet service with customers in 2024, following the launch of its first production satellites. Dave Limp, Amazon's senior vice president of devices and services, announced this timeline and showcased prototype user terminals, including a compact seven-inch antenna, at a recent satellite industry trade show. The company is investing over $10 billion in this ambitious internet-from-space venture.

title: Amazon Fails to Dismiss California Suit Over Inflated Prices
summary: A California state court judge tentatively denied Amazon's request to dismiss an antitrust lawsuit. The lawsuit, filed by California Attorney General Rob Bonta, accuses Amazon of forcing third-party sellers into agreements that result in "artificially high prices" for consumers. These agreements allegedly bar sellers from offering lower prices on other platforms and impose penalties for non-compliance.

title: 7 Cloud Computing Stocks That Can Make You a Millionaire as Data Explodes
summary: The article highlights seven cloud computing stocks—Salesforce, Microsoft, Snowflake, Amazon, IBM, Veeva Systems, and Alphabet—that are poised for growth as the demand for data storage and processing continues to explode. Despite a challenging 2022 for tech stocks, the public cloud sector demonstrated significant growth, indicating a strong migration of data to the cloud. Each company is detailed with its market position, recent financial performance, and reasons for its potential as a millionaire-maker investment.

title: 7 Kinds of Telehealth Care You Can Get Through Alexa
summary: Amazon's Alexa has evolved beyond simple requests to offer a range of telehealth services, partnering with organizations like Teladoc and One Medical for virtual doctor visits and primary care. Users can manage prescriptions via Amazon Pharmacy, utilize Alexa Together for remote caregiving, and access medical information and reminders through Mayo Clinic First Aid and WebMD skills. The integration of telemedicine with voice assistants aims to make healthcare more accessible and convenient for minor illnesses and ongoing health management.

title: eBay Inc. stock falls Wednesday, underperforms market
summary: eBay Inc. (EBAY) stock fell by 0.85% on Wednesday, closing at $40.81, and underperformed the broader market, which also saw declines in the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. The company's shares are currently $19.58 below their 52-week high. Competitors such as Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) and Walmart Inc. (WMT) experienced gains on the same day.

title: The Honest Company reports near-flat sales growth, indicating slowing demand
summary: The Honest Company reported near-flat sales growth in Q4 2022, with revenue increasing by only 2% to $81.9 million, and net losses rising. This performance, along with similar struggles at Grove Collaborative, highlights challenges for sustainable CPG startups in a market impacted by inflation and shifting consumer behaviors. New CEO Carla Vernón plans to improve profitability by focusing on margin improvement, bottom-of-the-funnel marketing, and expanding brick-and-mortar presence.

title: Kohl’s marketplace gives Lands’ End a much-needed boost
summary: Lands’ End reported a 4.6% year-over-year decline in Q4 net revenue, with global e-commerce down 6.1%. However, its third-party net revenue, which includes sales on marketplaces like Kohl's, rose 8%, significantly boosting the brand. Lands’ End plans to expand its presence on other marketplaces, including Macy's, acknowledging the potential for customer acquisition among lapsed and new customers.

title: IRS to crack down on income earned by third-party sellers on eBay, Amazon and other sites
summary: The IRS is changing its reporting rules for third-party sellers on platforms like eBay and Amazon, requiring companies to issue 1099 forms for transactions exceeding $600, eliminating the previous $20,000 sales threshold. This move aims to ensure that income from online sales is properly taxed. The article highlights a case where an individual was wrongly accused of undeclared sales, demonstrating potential identity theft issues that sellers might face.

title: Quantum Bits: IBM-Cleveland Clinic Launch; D-Wave Adds Solver; DOE/AWS Offer QICK
summary: IBM has launched its first Quantum System One at the Cleveland Clinic for medical research, aiming to integrate quantum with classical computing and AI to accelerate biomedical discoveries. Concurrently, D-Wave has released a new hybrid plug-in solver to simplify quantum functionality for machine learning workflows. Separately, AWS has made available the Quantum Instrumentation Control Kit (QICK), an open-source tool developed with DOE, Princeton, and the University of Chicago, designed to provide cloud-based access to experimental quantum hardware, fostering global collaboration in quantum research.

title: JD.com plans a self-operating warehouse in California
summary: JD.com is expanding its logistics operations in the U.S. by opening a third self-operating warehouse and distribution center in California. This new facility will add over 300 jobs and increase the company's warehouse footprint in the state to 1.3 million square feet. The e-commerce giant aims to leverage its automation capabilities to improve operating efficiency and work towards offering two-day delivery across the entire United States.

title: Online Cooking Class Market To See Extraordinary Growth : Udemy, Delish, Yanka Industries, Rouxbe
summary: Advance Market Analytics has published a new research publication on the "Online Cooking Class - Market Insights, to 2028", highlighting new evolving trends, drivers, restraints, and opportunities. The report identifies key players like Udemy, Delish, Yanka Industries, and Rouxbe, and details the market's segmentation by application, training type, cuisine, and experience level. The growth of the online cooking class market is driven by increasing online activities, the emergence of phone and online technology, and the flexibility and reduced cost structure of pre-recorded classes.

title: Amazon deepens tech-sector gloom with another 9,000 layoffs
summary: Amazon announced an additional 9,000 job cuts, primarily in its highly profitable cloud and advertising divisions, bringing its recent total layoffs to 27,000 corporate employees. This decision, attributed to economic uncertainty and the need for a more streamlined cost structure, follows similar large-scale layoffs across the tech sector by companies like Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms. CEO Andy Jassy explained that the cuts are a result of ongoing analysis of priorities and future economic uncertainties, impacting even the company's streaming unit, Twitch.

title: Amazon to Cut 9,000 More Jobs, Deepening Biggest Pullback Ever
summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy announced an additional 9,000 job cuts, primarily impacting Amazon Web Services, human resources, advertising, and Twitch. These new layoffs deepen the company's largest-ever reduction in workforce, following an initial round of 18,000 workers laid off starting in November. The announcement was made internally, with the cuts expected to occur in the coming weeks.

title: Consumer Staples ETF ‘XLP’ Outperforms Through Inflation Wave
summary: The Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLP) has outperformed during a period of high inflation, indicating a shift in consumer spending towards basic necessities. This is in contrast to the Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLY), which has suffered from reduced discretionary spending. The article suggests that while inflation has driven XLP's outperformance, receding oil prices could eventually lead to changes in consumer prices and spending habits.

title: For Broad-Based Large-Cap ESG Exposure, See CVLC
summary: The article highlights the Calvert US Large-Cap Core Responsible Index ETF (CVLC) as a significant option for investors seeking broad-based large-cap ESG exposure, particularly focusing on climate change and net-zero goals. It emphasizes CVLC's ability to identify companies taking actual steps towards net-zero objectives, citing examples like Apple, Amazon, and Tesla. The ETF offers a tangible way for investors to align their portfolios with values related to environmental sustainability and responsible investing.

title: Consider CVLC for Broad-Based, Large-Cap ESG Exposure
summary: The Calvert US Large-Cap Core Responsible Index ETF (CVLC) offers investors broad exposure to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) principles, particularly focusing on climate change and net-zero trends. Launched in February by Morgan Stanley Investment Management, CVLC includes companies like Apple, Amazon, and Tesla that are actively pursuing net-zero goals. The ETF helps investors identify companies genuinely committed to ESG, making it a relevant option as net-zero becomes an increasingly important investment criterion.

title: Gap pumps brakes on retail media unit
summary: Gap has decided to pause its retail media unit, GPS Media, after just over a year of operation, shifting resources to logistics and fulfillment instead. This move highlights the challenges faced by retailers in the rapidly growing but highly competitive retail media market, dominated by larger players like Amazon and Walmart. Despite the overall growth in retail media, Gap's struggles suggest that an established e-commerce presence alone does not guarantee success in this specialized advertising sector.

title: CVS Health Corp. stock underperforms Thursday when compared to competitors
summary: CVS Health Corp. (CVS) stock decreased by 2.74% on Thursday, closing at $72.37, despite an overall positive trading day for the stock market. This marks the second consecutive day of losses for CVS, and its stock is now significantly below its 52-week high. The company's performance was mixed compared to competitors, with Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) rising, while UnitedHealth Group Inc. (UNH) and Elevance Health Inc. (ELV) also experienced declines.

title: Digital Economy Discovers a Potential Frontier for Growth Thanks to Generative AI
summary: Generative AI, exemplified by large language models like GPT-3, is revolutionizing artificial intelligence, offering significant leaps in capabilities, speed, and cost-effectiveness. This new wave of AI is poised to drive massive innovation, boosting productivity and creating new applications across various sectors. The article explores how this technology will particularly impact and create opportunities in cloud computing, cybersecurity, and digital media, leading to substantial investment and growth in these areas.

title: Diversity in Business Awards honoree: Brian Kenner - Washington Business Journal
summary: Brian Kenner, the head of HQ2 Policy for Amazon.com Inc., has been recognized as a Diversity in Business Awards honoree by the Washington Business Journal. Kenner previously served as the D.C. deputy mayor for planning and economic development. This article highlights his current role at Amazon.

title: 15 Best E.L.F. Makeup and Skincare Products to Shop
summary: This article highlights 15 top E.L.F. Cosmetics makeup and skincare products, all priced at $50 or less, catering to beauty enthusiasts on a budget. It covers a range of items from sunscreens and retinoid serums to primers, eyeshadows, and concealers, emphasizing the brand's commitment to affordability and quality. The featured products offer solutions for various skincare and makeup needs, illustrating why E.L.F. remains a popular choice for high-quality, inexpensive beauty essentials.

title: Amazon FSx & ONTAP – Total Economic Impact Reports ROI | NetApp Blog
summary: NetApp's blog post highlights a Forrester Consulting study on the Total Economic Impact of Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP. The study found that AWS customers achieved a 61% ROI and payback in less than 6 months by migrating to this service. Key benefits include significant technology cost savings, increased labor efficiency, and faster migration times, with customers praising its ease of use and security.

title: Focus: Amazon, other retailers revamp 'free' shipping as costs soar
summary: Online retailers, including Amazon, are revamping their "free" shipping policies as rising costs and a contracting e-commerce market drain profits. They are introducing new fees, raising minimum purchase requirements, and shifting more expenses to consumers. This shift reflects a broader trend where retailers are starting to resemble airlines, charging for previously free services to maintain profitability in a challenging economic environment.

title: Cryptocurrencies add nothing useful to society, says chip-maker Nvidia
summary: Nvidia's chief technology officer, Michael Kagan, stated that cryptocurrencies bring nothing useful to society, despite the high demand for Nvidia's processors for crypto mining. He contrasted this with the value of AI applications like ChatGPT, which he believes represent a more worthwhile use of processing power. Nvidia had previously taken steps to limit the use of its graphics cards for crypto mining to prioritize supply for AI researchers and gamers.

title: WPP acquires social influencer marketing agency Obviously, expanding tech-powered creator content capabilities
summary: WPP has acquired Obviously, a New York-based social influencer marketing agency with operations in San Francisco and Paris, founded by Mae Karwowski and Maxime Domain in 2014. This acquisition expands WPP's tech-powered creator content capabilities, integrating Obviously's proprietary platform and nearly 100-person team into VMLY&R's network. Obviously's advanced technology includes AI-driven predictive analytics and streamlined campaign management, positioning WPP to strengthen its influencer marketing offerings for clients in a rapidly growing market.

title: AMC Entertainment shares jump on report Amazon exploring a deal
summary: Shares of AMC Entertainment Holdings Inc (AMC.N) jumped as much as 21% following a report that Amazon.com Inc (AMZN.O) was exploring an acquisition of the theater chain. Amazon founder Jeff Bezos reportedly dispatched advisers to look into the deal, though both companies declined to comment. Industry analysts, like Wedbush Securities, expressed skepticism about the potential acquisition due to AMC's significant debt and inflated valuation.

title: The Walt Disney Co. will reportedly begin layoffs this week
summary: The Walt Disney Co. is set to begin its first round of layoffs this week, impacting employees as part of a larger plan to cut 7,000 jobs by summer. CEO Bob Iger stated that notifications would occur in three rounds, with the goal of saving $5.5 billion for the company. These job reductions follow a difficult period for Disney and align with recent layoffs seen across various industries.

title: GXO promises “shared warehousing made easy” with UK launch of GXO Direct
summary: GXO has launched GXO Direct in the UK, combining its flexible warehousing space with that of its acquisition, Clipper Logistics, to create one of the largest shared space offerings in the country. This new service aims to help businesses expand sales channels, achieve economies of scale, reduce costs, and minimize environmental impact. GXO Direct targets a range of customers, from large established businesses to rapidly expanding smaller brands, offering them access to GXO’s extensive resources, technology, and value-added services across 30 sites.

title: U.S. parcel volume dipped 2% in 2022 after a 6% rise in 2021
summary: U.S. parcel volume saw a 2% dip in 2022, following a significant 33% surge in 2020 and a 6% rise in 2021, according to Pitney Bowes. Despite this decline in volume, parcel carriers achieved record revenues totaling $198 billion. Pitney Bowes forecasts a rebound, projecting parcel volume to reach 28 billion by 2028.

title: FedEx slumps, Amazon slows and more takeaways from a top shipping index
summary: A new report from the Pitney Bowes Parcel Shipping Index reveals a 2.2% decline in U.S. parcel volumes in 2022, marking a shift after years of growth. Despite this, parcel revenues increased by 6.5% year-over-year due to inflation and higher surcharges. FedEx saw the steepest drop in volume, while Amazon Logistics' growth flattened, prompting both companies to adjust strategies, including cost-cutting and capacity adjustments.

title: Pitney Bowes Parcel Shipping Index Finds US Volumes One Year and One Billion Parcels Ahead of Pre-Pandemic Forecast
summary: The 2022 Pitney Bowes Parcel Shipping Index reveals that while US parcel volumes saw a 2% decrease in 2022, they remain significantly higher than pre-pandemic forecasts, being one year and 1.1 billion parcels ahead of earlier predictions. Carrier revenues reached a record-breaking $198 billion, a 6.5% increase from 2021, and Pitney Bowes forecasts US parcel volume to reach 28 billion by 2028 with a 5% CAGR. This indicates strong resilience and adaptation within the shipping industry despite economic challenges.

title: Rackspace Lays Off 275 Employees As Stock Hits Bottom
summary: Rackspace Technology announced it is laying off 275 employees, approximately 4% of its global workforce, due to an uncertain economic climate and the need to align its cost structure with business demands. This decision comes as the company's stock has plummeted by 84% over the past year, trading at a near-all-time low of $1.76 per share, and after reporting an $805 million net loss in 2022 and experiencing a ransomware attack in December. Rackspace joins a growing list of tech companies implementing significant layoffs in 2023 amid a broader industry downturn.

title: Federal Tech Market Veteran Tom Lash Takes Helm at Meadowgate Technologies
summary: Tom Lash, a veteran of the federal technology market with three decades of experience, has been appointed CEO of Meadowgate Technologies. In his new role, Lash will focus on aligning the IT contractor's strategy with the demands for system architectures and support services in the national security sector. His prior experience includes serving as general manager at Amazon Web Services and holding leadership positions at Leidos.

title: Austin startup Wonderbelly lands on Target shelves
summary: Wonderbelly, an Austin-based antacid company, has announced its products are now available on the shelves of select Target Corp. stores and through Target's website. Previously, Wonderbelly products were sold via Amazon and regional grocers like Wheatsville Co-op, Market Street, and Fresh Plus Grocery. This expansion marks a significant step for the Austin startup in broadening its retail presence.

title: Microsoft cuts over 500 jobs in another round of tech layoffs
summary: Microsoft has laid off 559 workers in Bellevue and Redmond, bringing their regional total to over 2,700 jobs cut since January. This follows a previous round of layoffs in February and reflects a broader trend of job cuts across the tech industry, with companies like Meta and Amazon also reducing their workforces. Overall, U.S. tech companies have shed more than 300,000 jobs in recent months.

title: W.W. Grainger Inc. stock rises Tuesday, outperforms market
summary: W.W. Grainger Inc. (GWW) stock rose 0.62% to $675.84 on Tuesday, outperforming the broader market which saw the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average decline. This marked the second consecutive day of gains for the stock, placing it $33.37 short of its 52-week high. The company also outperformed competitors like Amazon.com Inc., Home Depot Inc., and Lowe's Cos.

title: Synchrony mulls creating a digital wallet
summary: Synchrony Financial, a major provider of private label credit cards for retailers, is exploring the development of its own digital wallet while actively focusing on enhancing digital wallet services for its existing clients. The company aims to transition consumers from physical cards to more digital experiences, recognizing changing customer expectations and potential future revenue streams. Synchrony is currently integrating its digital cards into third-party wallets but is contemplating creating its own, although this move would require careful consideration of its partnerships and potential regulatory impacts.

title: Amazon targets multiple bad actors in novel lawsuit, further protecting selling partners from fraud
summary: Amazon has filed a novel lawsuit against multiple bad actors who submitted thousands of false copyright infringement claims to remove products and sellers from its store. This action by Amazon's Counterfeit Crimes Unit (CCU) aims to protect selling partners, customers, and brands, reinforcing the integrity of the Amazon store. The lawsuit builds on the existing Amazon Brand Registry program, which has already seen a 99% reduction in suspected infringement reports from enrolled brands.

title: Colgate Total Tackles the Root Cause of Oral Health Problems with New Innovation
summary: Colgate is introducing Colgate Total Plaque Pro-Release, a new toothpaste designed to significantly reduce harmful plaque bacteria and provide 24-hour antibacterial protection. This innovation aims to combat the root cause of oral health problems like bad breath, cavities, and gingivitis. The toothpaste utilizes Smart Foam Technology and Stannous Fluoride to penetrate hard-to-reach areas and improve long-term gum health, helping consumers feel "Dentist-Ready."

title: CVS Health Finalizes $8B Acquisition of Signify Health
summary: CVS Health has completed its $8 billion acquisition of home healthcare company Signify Health, accelerating its value-based care strategy. The merger aims to improve care delivery, lower costs, and enhance member engagement, particularly for Medicare Advantage beneficiaries. Signify Health's CEO, Kyle Armbrester, will continue to lead the company, which also includes Caravan Health.

title: How a Top T. Rowe Manager Keeps Beating the Markets
summary: David Giroux, manager of the T. Rowe Price Capital Appreciation fund, has consistently outperformed market indexes through a contrarian investment strategy. He zigs when others zag, buying undervalued assets like technology stocks in 2022 or utilities when they were lagging, and making strategic moves in the bond market. Giroux focuses on companies with strong fundamentals and skilled management, avoiding "value traps" and wisely allocating capital, as demonstrated by his successful investment in PNC Financial Services Group and avoidance of struggling regional banks.

title: Duration: Newmark sells 54,226 s/f retail for $26.4 million for Acadia Realty Trust to Benderson Development
summary: Newmark successfully brokered the sale of a 54,226 s/f retail asset located at 330-340 River St. in Cambridge, MA, from Acadia Realty Trust to Benderson Development for $26.4 million. The property includes a two-story Whole Foods Market and an adjacent Walgreens. This transaction highlights the strong demand for high-quality retail assets with solid tenants and affluent demographics, even in a challenging capital markets environment.

title: SPDR S&P 500 (SPY) Stock: Breakout Leveraging Tech Stocks Rally?
summary: The SPDR S&P 500 (SPY) ETF has shown a positive resurgence in 2023, largely driven by gains in tech and semiconductor stocks, which comprise a significant portion of its portfolio. Technical analysis suggests a potential bullish breakout for SPY, with indicators pointing to an upcoming rally. Investors are advised to watch support levels and anticipate a rise leveraging the strength of its underlying tech holdings.

title: Top and Flop ETFs of March
summary: The U.S. stock market experienced extreme volatility in March, characterized by bank failures and a tech-driven rally. This article highlights the top and flop ETFs of the month, with technology and gold-related funds performing well, while regional bank and natural gas ETFs saw declines.

title: Walmart Inc. stock rises Friday, still underperforms market
summary: Walmart Inc. stock (WMT) saw a 1.22% increase on Friday, closing at $147.45. Despite this rise and a positive trading day for the broader market, Walmart's stock underperformed the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average. The stock closed below its 52-week high and rose less than competitor Amazon.com Inc.
